sentences.text: This miscellaneous first appeal is filed by petitioner under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act (for short 'the Act'), seeking enhancement of compensation for the injuries sustained by him in a motor vehicle accident dated 12.04.2012.
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to by their rank before the Tribunal.

3. It is the case of the petitioner that on 12.04.2012 at about 10:30 p.m., on the main road near HDFC Bank, Sedam, petitioner was proceeding on motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-32-V-5546 ('motorcycle' for short).

A tanker lorry bearing Reg.No.KA-32-A-7434 ('offending vehicle' for short)
was proceeding in front of him in a rash or negligent manner.
The driver of offending vehicle suddenly applied break, due to which, the accident occurred and petitioner sustained grievous injuries resulting in permanent partial disability.
Despite prolonged treatment, petitioner is not completely cured.
As the owner and insurer, respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
4. Respondent No.1 has remained ex parte.

5. Respondent No.2 has filed written statement disputing that the accident occurred due to rash or negligent driving of offending vehicle, the age, occupation, income of the petitioner, nature of the injuries sustained by him and that they have resulted in permanent partial disability and also medical expenses incurred for the treatment.
At the time of accident, petitioner was drunk and thereby contributed to the accident.
Since the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding a valid driving licence, respondent No.2 is not liable to pay the compensation and prays to dismiss the appeal.
6. Based on the pleadings, the Tribunal has framed necessary issues.

7. Petitioner got himself examined as P.W.1 and the doctor as P.W.2 and relied upon Exs.P.1 to 20.
8.

Respondent No.2 has not led any oral evidence, but got marked the insurance policy certificate as Ex.D1.
9.
Vide the impugned judgment and award, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition filed by the petitioner granting compensation in a sum of Rs.2,68,825/-.

However, the Tribunal held that petitioner was equally responsible for the accident and therefore he is entitled for only 50% of the compensation with interest at 6% per annum and directed respondent No.2 to pay the same as detailed below:

10. Respondents have not challenged the impugned judgment and award.
11. During the course of arguments, learned counsel representing the petitioner submitted that the notional income considered by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
Having regard to the nature of the injuries sustained, the compensation granted under all the heads is on the lower side.

The Tribunal has erred in attributing 50%
negligence on the petitioner and prays to allow the appeal.
12. On the other hand, learned counsel for respondents supported the impugned judgment and award and prays for dismissal of the appeal.

sentences.text: 13. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned counsel for respondent No.2 and perused the records.

14. Having regard to the fact that the respondent has not challenged the impugned judgment and award, the findings of the Tribunal that the accident occurred also due to the rash or negligent driving by the driver of the offending vehicle and in the said accident, the petitioner sustained injuries has attained finality.

15. Appreciating the fact that while driving his two wheeler petitioner had not maintained the requisite distance and charge-sheet came to be filed against the driver of both offending vehicle and the petitioner and also the fact that medical records indicate that at the time of accident petitioner was drunk, the Tribunal is justified in holding that petitioner was also equally responsible for the accident and attributing 50% negligence on him.
The said findings does not call for any interference.

16. As on the date of accident, the petitioner was aged 34 years and therefore,
multiplier 16 taken by the Tribunal is correct.

In the absence of proof of exact income,
the Tribunal has taken his notional income at Rs.6,000/- .
Since the accident is of the year 2012, based on minimum wages, the notional income ought to have been taken at Rs.6,500/-.

The Tribunal has considered the disability at 13%, however, looking to the nature of injuries suffered and the fact that it has resulted in permanent partial disability, it would be reasonable to assess the disability at 17% of the whole body.
With these components, the loss of income due to disability is at Rs.6,500/- x 12 x 16 x 17% = 2,12,160/- as against Rs.1,49,760/- granted by the Tribunal.
17. Based on medical bills, compensation granted in a sum of Rs.59,065/- under the head medical expenses is correct.

At the rate of Rs.6,500/- for a period of three months petitioner is entitled compensation in a sum of Rs.19,500/- under the head loss of income during laid up period as against Rs.18,000- granted by the Tribunal.

18. Having regard to the nature of the injuries sustained, the period of treatment and that it has resulted in permanent partial disability, the compensation granted in a sum of Rs.20,000/- under the head pain & suffering, Rs.12,000/- under the head attendant charges, food nutrition and miscellaneous and Rs.10,000/- under the head loss of amenities is on the lower side and the same is enhanced to Rs.40,000/-,
30,000/- and 25,000/-
respectively.

19. Thus, in all the petitioner is entitled for total compensation in a sum of Rs.3,85,725/- together with interest at 6% p.a. as against Rs.2,68,825/- granted by the Tribunal as detailed below:

ORDER (i) The Appeal is allowed in part.

(iii) Respondent No.2/insurance company shall deposit 50% of the compensation amount together with interest at 6% p.a. within a period of six weeks from the date of this order (minus the compensation, if any, already paid/deposited).
